prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” argues the Conservatives have “broken Britain” and Labour would “bankrupt” it. The party proposes a rapid, costed reform agenda focused on border control, lower taxes, NHS reform, law and order, and scrapping Net Zero, claiming to restore sovereignty, culture, and economic growth.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration and stop small boats, including detain-and-deport and, if needed, returning boats to France.
- Zero NHS waiting lists while remaining free at point of use; cut back‑office waste; tax breaks and training reforms to tackle staffing.
- Make work pay by lifting the income tax threshold to £20,000; higher-rate from £70,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping levies and Net Zero; expand UK oil and gas.
- Broader “common sense” reforms across policing, education, justice, defence, housing, families, and infrastructure.

Key policy areas (first 100 days focus, then longer-term)
- Immigration: Leave the ECHR; create a Department of Immigration; bar asylum claims from safe countries; offshore processing; immediate deportation of foreign criminals; bar student dependents; five-year residency/employment before benefits; an Employer Immigration Tax on hiring foreign workers (exempt small firms and essential health/care staff).
- Government waste: Stop paying interest on QE reserves; 5% efficiency savings across departments; cut foreign aid by 50%; reduce retained EU laws; improve HMRC tax collection.
- Economy (personal): Raise thresholds; cut fuel duty 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy and green levies; cut stamp duty (0% to £750k); abolish VAT tourist tax; reform inheritance tax (0% up to £2m, 20% above).
- Economy (business): Lift corporation tax threshold to £100k; reduce main rate to 20%, then 15%; abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high-street SMEs with a 4% online delivery tax; planning and deregulation push.
- NHS: Zero basic-rate tax for NHS/social care frontline staff for three years; end medical training caps; student fee write-offs for service; use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; voucher guarantees if GP/consultant/surgery waits exceed targets; efficiency drives and Pharmacy First.
- Energy/Net Zero: Scrap Net Zero and subsidies; fast-track North Sea and shale test sites; expand SMRs and other technologies.
- Policing/Justice: Recruit 40,000 officers; zero-tolerance policing; more stop and search; remove DEI roles; tougher sentencing (automatic life for violent repeat offenders); expand prison places; increase justice budget to reduce backlogs; redefine hate crime.
- Education: “Patriotic” curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap student loan interest; stricter university entry; expand PRUs; protect free speech.
- Benefits: Two-strike rule for job offers; face‑to‑face assessments; targeted return‑to‑work support, especially ages 16–34.
- Brexit/sovereignty: Scrap retained EU law; abandon the Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the Trade and Cooperation Agreement; reject WHO treaty/WEF influence; oppose CBDC.
- Defence: Raise spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% within 6 years; pay review; legal protections; a veterans department; recruit 30,000 for the army; procurement reform.
- Housing: Fast-track brownfield; prioritize locals for social housing; scrap Section 24 for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill.
- Families: Larger transferable marriage allowance (as finances allow); front‑load child benefit for ages 1–4; mandate single‑sex spaces; push child‑safe smartphones.
- Transport/utilities: Scrap HS2; end ULEZ/LTNs; focus investment on coastal, northern, Welsh and Midlands links; new utility model (50% public, 50% UK pensions), cap standing charges.
- Agriculture/Fishing: Boost farm budget; scrap climate‑related subsidies; protect country sports; empower CMA on supermarket pricing; “Buy British”; police the UK EEZ; ban foreign supertrawlers; rebuild processing and fleets.
- Pensions/Social care: Royal Commission on social care; curb offshore tax practices; pension system review; fix Mineworkers’ scheme.
- Constitutional: Leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; restrict postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights; reform BBC; anti-corruption unit.

Funding
- Claimed annual savings: £150bn plus £10bn from assumed extra growth = £160bn.
- Claimed annual costs: £141bn.
